mainTopic: The morning תמיד service: opening the היכל, the far-reaching sounds and smells of the מקדש, cleaning the inner מזבח and the מנורה, and the binding, שחיטה and blood service of the lamb.
overview: This amud is all משנה and follows the early-morning service in the מקדש. The תמיד lamb is checked again by torchlight. The כהנים who clear the inner מזבח and the מנורה go ahead with a basket, a jug and two keys. They enter the היכל through the northern side door, because a פסוק in יחזקאל keeps the southern one shut. Then they open the great gate, and the שוחט waits to hear it open. The משנה lists the מקדש sounds that could be heard from יריחו, and even the smell of the קטורת that made goats sneeze far away. Next the lamb is brought to the בית המטבחיים, and the inner מזבח and the מנורה are cleaned, ending the פרק with a הדרן. The new פרק explains how the lamb is bound and where it is slaughtered, and how its blood is placed on the מזבח.

steps.title: The lamb is checked again by torchlight
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its earlier line about giving the lamb water from a gold cup, then rules that the lamb is checked again by torchlight even though it was already checked the evening before.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The lamb was given water from a cup] of gold. Even though it was already checked the evening before, they check it again by the light of torches.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its description of preparing the תמיד lamb. It says the lamb gets a second check for מומין in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamb was already found free of blemishes the night before. Even so, the משנה requires a fresh check right before it is used. Since it is still dark, the check is done by torchlight.

keyTerms.meaning: Already checked and found free of blemishes

phrases.english: Of gold.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מְבוּקָּר מִבָּעֶרֶב –
phrases.english: Even though it was already checked in the evening,
they check it again by the light of torches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא מְבוּקָּר מִבָּעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier משנה about preparing the תמיד lamb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תמיד lamb is checked again in the morning by torchlight, even though it was already checked the evening before.

steps.title: The ash-clearing כהנים go first with four vessels
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the כהנים who won the jobs of clearing the inner מזבח and the מנורה go ahead early, carrying four vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ones who won the clearing of ashes from the inner altar and from the מנורה would go ahead first, holding four vessels: the basket, the jug and two keys.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It introduces the כהנים in charge of cleaning the inner מזבח and the מנורה, and lists the four tools they carry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These jobs were given out by lottery, which is why the משנה says 'who won.' These כהנים go ahead of the others. The משנה only lists the four tools here and describes them in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (golden) altar for incense, inside the היכל

phrases.english: The one who won the clearing of ashes from the inner altar
and the clearing of ashes from the מנורה
would go ahead first,
with four vessels in their hands:
the basket, the jug, and two keys.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁזָּכָה בְּדִישּׁוּן מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי וּבְדִישּׁוּן הַמְּנוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and moves from the lamb to the work inside the היכל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים who clear the inner מזבח and the מנורה go first, carrying a basket, a jug and two keys.

steps.title: What the basket and the jug looked like
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the first two vessels: the basket looks like a large gold measure but holds two and a half קבין, and the jug looks like a big gold flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: The basket looks like a gold vessel the size of a three-קב measure, but it holds two and a half קבין. The jug looks like a large gold flask.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the first two of the four vessels it just listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basket looks like a vessel that holds three קבין, but it actually holds only two and a half. The jug is compared to a large gold flask so we can picture its size.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure equal to three קבין

phrases.english: The basket looks like a gold three-קב vessel,
but it holds two and a half קבין.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַכּוּז – דּוֹמֶה לְקִיתוֹן גָּדוֹל שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: And the jug looks like a large gold flask.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַטְּנִי – דּוֹמֶה לְתַרְקַב שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains two of the vessels listed in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The basket looks like a three-קב gold vessel but holds two and a half קבין. The jug looks like a large gold flask.

steps.title: How the two keys worked
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the two keys: with one, the כהן reached in up to his armpit to open a lock from the inside, and the other opened its lock directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two keys: with one, he reaches his arm down up to the armpit, and the other opens directly.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes explaining the four vessels by describing how each key was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first lock was on the inside of the door. To open it, the כהן had to push his arm through an opening all the way up to his armpit. The second key opened its lock directly, with no reaching in.

keyTerms.meaning: The armpit (reaching in arm's length up to the armpit)

phrases.english: And the two keys:
one, with which he reaches in up to the armpit,
and one which opens directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁתֵּי מַפְתְּחוֹת – אֶחָד שֶׁהוּא יוֹרֵד בְּאַמַּת הַשֶּׁחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes describing the four vessels from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One key opened a lock from the inside by reaching in up to the armpit, and the other opened its lock directly.

steps.title: The two side doors of the great gate
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the כהן comes to the northern side door. The great gate had two side doors, north and south, and nobody ever entered through the southern one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to the northern side door. The great gate had two side doors, one in the north and one in the south. Nobody entered through the southern one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה follows the כהן's route. It explains why he goes to the northern side door: nobody used the southern one. This sets up the proof from יחזקאל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The great gate of the היכל had a small side door (פשפש) on each side. Only the northern one was used. The reason for the southern one being closed comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A small side door (wicket) next to a big gate
The great gate of the היכל

phrases.english: He came to the northern side door.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי פִּשְׁפָּשִׁין הָיוּ לוֹ לַשַּׁעַר הַגָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: The great gate had two side doors,
one in the north and one in the south.
Through the southern one, no person ever entered.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא לוֹ לַפִּשְׁפָּשׁ הַצְּפוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the route of the כהנים from step 2, who now head toward the היכל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of the great gate's two side doors, only the northern one was used. Nobody entered through the southern one.

steps.title: A פסוק in יחזקאל about the closed southern door
steps.stepSummary: The משנה supports the rule that nobody entered the southern side door with a פסוק in יחזקאל: this gate shall stay shut, because ה׳ entered through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: About this door, יחזקאל made it clear, as it says: 'And ה׳ said to me: This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter by it, for ה׳ the God of Israel has entered by it, and it shall be shut.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a פסוק to back up what it just said: the southern side door was never used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a certain gate must stay closed and no person may enter it, because ה׳ entered through it. The משנה applies this to the southern side door, which explains why it was always kept shut.

phrases.aramaic: עָלָיו הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ עַל יְדֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל,
phrases.english: About it, it was made clear by יחזקאל,
as it says: 'And ה׳ said to me:

phrases.aramaic: הַשַּׁעַר הַזֶּה סָגוּר יִהְיֶה לֹא יִפָּתֵחַ
phrases.english: This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened,
and no man shall enter by it,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּא בוֹ
phrases.english: for ה׳, the God of Israel, has entered by it,
and it shall be shut.'

steps.triggerLanguage: עָלָיו הוּא מְפוֹרָשׁ עַל יְדֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 5's rule that the southern side door was never used.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that nobody entered the southern side door of the great gate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 44:2: 'This gate shall be shut... no man shall enter by it, for ה׳... has entered by it.'

steps.title: The כהן's path through the chamber into the היכל
steps.stepSummary: The כהן takes the key, opens the northern side door, goes into the small chamber, then into the היכל, and walks until he reaches the great gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the key and opened the side door, entered the chamber, and from the chamber went into the היכל, until he reached the great gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to the כהן's route. It follows him step by step from the side door to the inside of the great gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side door leads into a small chamber (תא), and that chamber leads into the היכל. This is where the two keys from step 4 get used. Now the כהן is inside, standing at the great gate, which is locked from the inside.

phrases.aramaic: נָטַל אֶת הַמַּפְתֵּחַ וּפָתַח אֶת הַפִּשְׁפָּשׁ,
phrases.english: He took the key and opened the side door,
and entered the chamber,
and from the chamber into the היכל,
until he reaches the great gate.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל אֶת הַמַּפְתֵּחַ וּפָתַח אֶת הַפִּשְׁפָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side point about the southern door, the משנה goes back to the route that started in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן enters through the northern side door, passes through the chamber into the היכל, and reaches the great gate from inside.

steps.title: Opening the great gate
steps.stepSummary: At the great gate, the כהן removes the bolt and the locks and opens it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he reached the great gate, he removed the bolt and the locks and opened it.
steps.whatsHappening: The כהן unlocks the great gate from the inside and opens it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The great gate was held shut by a bar (the נגר) and by locks that held the bar in place. The כהן removes both and opens the gate. That is why he had to go in through the side door first.

keyTerms.meaning: A bolt or bar that locks a door
Locks (here, the ones holding the bolt in place)

phrases.english: When he reached the great gate,
he removed the bolt and the locks
and opened it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ לְשַׁעַר הַגָּדוֹל, הֶעֱבִיר אֶת הַנֶּגֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues directly from step 7: now that he is at the gate, he opens it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן removes the bolt and locks and opens the great gate from the inside.

steps.title: The שוחט waits to hear the great gate open
steps.stepSummary: The שוחט of the תמיד does not slaughter until he hears the great gate open.
steps.simpleTranslation: The slaughterer would not slaughter until he heard that the great gate had been opened.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה links the gate-opening to the שחיטה of the תמיד: the שחיטה waits for the sound of the great gate opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule sets the order of events. The opening of the היכל's great gate comes first, and only then is the תמיד slaughtered. The משנה here gives the rule but not the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who slaughters the קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: The morning order: the lamb is checked again by torchlight. The ash-clearing כהנים go first with a basket, a jug and two keys. They enter through the northern side door, since the southern one stays shut because of the פסוק in יחזקאל. They open the great gate from inside, and only after it is heard opening is the תמיד slaughtered.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the שחיטה of the תמיד depends on the היכל being opened first.

phrases.english: The slaughterer would not slaughter
until he heard that the great gate had been opened.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הָיָה שׁוֹחֵט הַשּׁוֹחֵט עַד שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵעַ שַׁעַר גָּדוֹל שֶׁנִּפְתַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the gate-opening from step 8 to the start of the שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תמיד is not slaughtered until the שוחט hears the great gate open.

steps.title: מקדש sounds heard from יריחו, part one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that from יריחו people could hear the great gate opening, the מגריפה, the Levites' שיר, בן ארזה's cymbal, and the חליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: From יריחו they heard the great gate open, the מגריפה, the singing of the לוים, בן ארזה's cymbal, and the חליל.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a list of sounds from the בית המקדש that were loud enough to be heard far away in יריחו. It begins with the great gate opening, which connects to the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the שוחט waited to hear the great gate open. Now the משנה adds how loud that gate was: it could be heard all the way in יריחו. It then lists more loud Temple sounds in the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: Jericho, a city far from ירושלים
A shovel-shaped instrument in the מקדש that made a loud noise
The song the לוים sang in the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how strong the presence of the מקדש was. Its sounds reached far beyond ירושלים.

phrases.english: From Jericho they would hear
the sound of the great gate being opened.
From Jericho they would hear the sound of the shovel instrument.
From Jericho they would hear the sound of the song.
From Jericho they would hear
the sound of ben Arza clashing the cymbal.
From Jericho they would hear the sound of the flute.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִירִיחוֹ הָיוּ שׁוֹמְעִין קוֹל שַׁעַר גָּדוֹל שֶׁנִּפְתַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the opening of the great gate by describing how far its sound carried.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The great gate, the מגריפה, the שיר, the cymbal and the חליל could all be heard from יריחו.

steps.title: מקדש sounds heard from יריחו, part two
steps.stepSummary: The list goes on: גביני the כרוז, בן קטין's wooden machine for the כיור, the שיר, and the שופר. יש אומרים: even the כהן גדול saying השם on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From יריחו they also heard גביני the crier, בן קטין's wooden machine for the כיור, the singing and the שופר. Some say they even heard the כהן גדול saying השם on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same list of loud Temple sounds. At the end, a second opinion adds one more sound: the voice of the כהן גדול on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line keeps the same pattern, 'מיריחו היו שומעין.' The יש אומרים opinion goes a step further. It says even a single human voice, the כהן גדול saying השם, reached יריחו.

keyTerms.meaning: Crier, the one who called out announcements in the מקדש
The basin the כהנים washed their hands and feet from
Says ה׳'s special name out loud

phrases.aramaic: מִירִיחוֹ הָיוּ שׁוֹמְעִין קוֹל גְּבִינִי כָּרוֹז.
phrases.english: From Jericho they would hear the voice of Gevini the crier.
From Jericho they would hear
the sound of the wood that ben Katin made
into a machine for the basin.
From Jericho they would hear the sound of the song.
From Jericho they would hear the sound of the shofar.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים אַף קוֹלוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: And some say: even the voice of the High Priest
at the time he says the Name
on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִירִיחוֹ הָיוּ שׁוֹמְעִין קוֹל גְּבִינִי כָּרוֹז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sounds heard from יריחו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: More Temple sounds reached יריחו. According to יש אומרים, even the כהן גדול's voice on יום הכפורים did.

steps.title: The smell of the קטורת reached יריחו
steps.stepSummary: The משנה moves from sounds to smell: people in יריחו could smell the פיטום הקטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From יריחו they could smell the קטורת being prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches from things heard to something smelled. The smell of the קטורת also reached יריחו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same phrase 'מיריחו' is kept, but now it is about smell instead of sound. This sets up the next step, where a sage gives a personal story to support it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ground spice mixture of the incense

phrases.english: From Jericho they would smell
the scent of the incense mixture.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִירִיחוֹ הָיוּ מְרֵיחִין רֵיחַ פִּיטּוּם הַקְּטוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'from Jericho' list from sound to smell.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The smell of the קטורת reached יריחו.

steps.title: Goats sneezing from the incense smell
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן דגלאי says his father's goats in the mountains of מכוור used to sneeze from the smell of the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן דגלאי said: my father had goats in the mountains of מכוור, and they would sneeze from the smell of the קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: A sage tells a story from his own family to back up the claim that the קטורת's smell traveled very far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 only stated that the smell reached far away. רבי אלעזר בן דגלאי adds real-life evidence: animals in a far-off place actually reacted to it. This supports the claim and even suggests the smell was strong.

keyTerms.meaning: The mountains of מכוור, a place far from ירושלים

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Diglai said:
My father had goats
in the (cities) [mountains] of Mikhvar,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'cities of מכוור'. The corrected wording in square brackets says 'mountains of מכוור'.

phrases.english: and they would sneeze
from the scent of the incense mixture.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דִּגְלַאי עִזִּים הָיוּ לְאַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 12 with a firsthand story.
steps.raayaObject: That the smell of the קטורת traveled very far from the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The family story of רבי אלעזר בן דגלאי about his father's goats sneezing far away.
steps.whatToRemember: The מקדש's sounds and smells reached far beyond ירושלים: gate, music, shofar, and the קטורת whose smell made goats sneeze.

steps.title: Bringing the תמיד to the slaughterhouse
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the כהן who won the lottery for the תמיד pulls it to the בית המטבחיים, and the כהנים who won the אברים go with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The priest who won the daily offering pulls it along to the slaughterhouse, and the priests who won the limbs go with him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה goes back to the order of the morning service. The lamb for the תמיד is brought to the place where it will be slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gate is now open (steps 8-9), so the slaughter can begin. The משנה tells us who moves the lamb: the winner of the lottery for the תמיד. The כהנים who will later carry the limbs walk along with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Won, meaning won the lottery for a job
The daily קרבן brought every morning and afternoon
The slaughtering area in the עזרה

phrases.english: The one who won the daily offering
phrases.notes: He means the כהן who won the lottery for the job of slaughtering the תמיד.

phrases.english: pulls it and goes to the slaughterhouse.
And those who won the limbs
go with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁזָּכָה בַּתָּמִיד מְשָׁכוֹ וְהוֹלֵךְ בְּבֵית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side note about יריחו, the משנה returns to the order of the תמיד service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The winner of the תמיד lottery leads the lamb to the בית המטבחיים, and the winners of the אברים go with him.

steps.title: What the slaughterhouse looked like
steps.stepSummary: The בית המטבחיים was north of the מזבח. It had eight short pillars with cedar beams on top, three rows of iron hooks on each for hanging the animal, and marble tables between the pillars for skinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The slaughterhouse was north of the altar. It had eight short pillars with cedar blocks on top and iron hooks in them, three rows on each, for hanging and skinning the animals on marble tables between the pillars.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה pauses to describe the setup of the slaughtering area, so we can picture where the תמיד is hung and skinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a physical description, not an argument. Each part has a job. The pillars hold cedar blocks, the iron hooks hold up the slaughtered animal, and the marble tables are where the skinning is done.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִים הָיָה לִצְפוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: The slaughterhouse was to the north of the altar,
and by it were eight short pillars,
and squares of cedar on top of them,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֻנְקְלָאוֹת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל הָיוּ קְבוּעִין בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: and iron hooks were fixed in them,
and three rows on each and every one,
on which they hang and skin

phrases.aramaic: עַל שׁוּלְחָנוֹת שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ שֶׁבֵּין הָעַמּוּדִים.
phrases.english: on marble tables that were between the pillars.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִים הָיָה לִצְפוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the place the תמיד was just brought to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית המטבחיים, north of the מזבח, had pillars, cedar blocks, iron hooks in three rows, and marble tables for hanging and skinning.
steps.whatToRemember: The תמיד is pulled to the בית המטבחיים north of the מזבח, where it is hung on iron hooks and skinned on marble tables.

steps.title: Clearing the ashes from the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: The כהן who won דישון מזבח הפנימי goes in, puts a basket in front of himself, scoops the ashes into it by the handful, sweeps in the rest, leaves the basket, and goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן who won the job of clearing ashes from the inner מזבח went in and took the basket. He put it in front of himself and kept scooping handfuls of ash into it. At the end he swept the leftover ash into it, set the basket down, and went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now describes the next morning job inside the היכל: clearing the ashes off the inner, golden מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The work has two stages. First he scoops the ash by the handful, and at the end he sweeps in the small amount that is left. Notice that he leaves the basket inside the היכל when he goes out instead of carrying it away.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל, where the קטורת is burned
Scooping with the hands, by the handful

phrases.english: The one who won the removal of ash from the inner altar
entered and took the basket,
and placed it in front of him,
and would scoop handfuls and put them into it.
And at the end, he swept the rest into it,
and set it down and went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁזָּכָה בְּדִישּׁוּן מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the slaughter area in the עזרה back into the היכל. It picks up the ash-clearing כהן from step 2, who now uses the basket described in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner מזבח is cleared by scooping its ashes into a basket and then sweeping in the rest. The basket is left inside.

steps.title: Cleaning the lamps of the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: The כהן who won דישון המנורה cleans the lamps. If the two eastern lamps are still lit, he cleans the others and leaves those two burning. If they have gone out, he cleans them and relights them from the lamps that are burning, and only afterward cleans the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן who won the job of cleaning the מנורה went in. If he found the two eastern lamps still burning, he cleaned out the rest and left those two burning in their place. If he found that they had gone out, he cleaned them out, lit them from the lamps that were still burning, and after that cleaned out the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the second job inside the היכל, cleaning the מנורה. It gives two cases, depending on whether the two eastern lamps are still lit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order changes with the case. If the two lamps are lit, they are left alone and only the others are cleaned. If they went out, they are handled first: cleaned and relit from lamps that are still burning, before the others are cleaned. That way he still has burning lamps to light them from.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden candelabrum in the היכל
Cleans out the old ash and burnt wick from a lamp

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read "מזרחית מערבית" as two lamps at opposite ends of the מנורה. It is describing the two eastern lamps, and the second of them is the one called the "western lamp."

phrases.english: The one who won the removal of ash from the menorah,
entered, and if he found two lamps,
the easternmost one and the "western" one, burning –
phrases.notes: These are the two eastern lamps. The second one is the lamp known as the "western lamp."

phrases.english: he cleans out the rest,
and leaves these burning in their place.
If he found that they had gone out –
he cleans them out and lights them from the burning ones,
and afterward he cleans out the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁזָּכָה בְּדִישּׁוּן הַמְּנוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second job done inside the היכל, right after the inner מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lit eastern lamps are left burning and the others are cleaned. Lamps that went out are cleaned and relit from the burning ones first, and then the rest are cleaned.

steps.title: The three-step stone in front of the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: There was a stone with three steps in front of the מנורה. The כהן stood on it to prepare the lamps, put the jug down on the second step, and went out.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a stone in front of the מנורה with three steps in it. The כהן stood on it to prepare the lamps. He put the jug on the second step and went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a physical detail: the stepped stone the כהן used to reach the lamps, and where he left his jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps let the כהן stand up high enough to work on the lamps. Just like the basket at the inner מזבח, the jug is left behind inside, here on the second step, before he goes out.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepares the lamps (cleans them and gets them ready)
A jug, used to hold the cleaned-out ashes and wicks

phrases.english: And there was a stone in front of the menorah,
and it had three steps

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעָלֶיהָ כֹּהֵן עוֹמֵד וּמֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת,
phrases.english: on which the כהן stands and prepares the lamps,
he placed the jug
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, "he placed."

phrases.english: on the second step, and went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶבֶן הָיְתָה לִפְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the setting and the closing action for the מנורה job.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן works on the lamps from a three-step stone, and he leaves the jug on the second step.
steps.whatToRemember: Both jobs inside the היכל end the same way: the container of ashes (the basket or the jug) is left inside, and the כהן goes out.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אמר להם הממונה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק called אמר להם הממונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אמר להם הממונה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק אמר להם הממונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional way of saying goodbye to a פרק and expressing the hope to come back and learn it again. It does not teach any new law.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you," said when finishing a פרק
The officer in charge of the כהנים, whose words open this פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The appointed officer said to them"

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ אָמַר לָהֶם הַמְמוּנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק אמר להם הממונה ends with the morning work inside the היכל: the inner מזבח and the מנורה.

steps.title: How the lamb was bound and held
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens. The lamb was not tied with all its legs together (כפיתה). It was bound in the way called עקידה. The כהנים who won the limbs held it, with its head to the south and its face to the west. The שוחט stood on the east, facing west.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not tie up the lamb's legs all together. Instead they bound it. The כהנים who won the limbs held onto it. This is how it was bound: its head to the south and its face to the west. The slaughterer stood on the east side, facing west.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה that describes how the תמיד lamb was prepared for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts two ways of tying an animal and says only one was used. It also tells us who held the lamb: the same כהנים who later carry its limbs. It then gives the exact positions of the animal and of the שוחט.

keyTerms.meaning: Tying up the animal's legs all together
Binding the animal (עקידה), a different way of tying it
The limbs of the offering, which כהנים won in the lottery
The one who slaughters the animal

phrases.english: Mishnah:
They would not tie up the lamb,
phrases.notes: Tying up means binding all four legs together.

phrases.english: rather, they would bind it.
phrases.notes: This is עקידה: a front leg tied to a back leg, the way יצחק was bound.

phrases.english: Those who won the limbs hold onto it.
And this was how it was bound:
its head to the south, and its face to the west.
And the slaughterer stands on the east,
and his face is toward the west.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא הָיוּ כּוֹפְתִין אֶת הַטָּלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the הדרן of פרק אמר להם הממונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תמיד lamb is bound with עקידה, not כפיתה. The כהנים who won the limbs hold it, head south and face west, and the שוחט stands east, facing west.

steps.title: Where the morning and afternoon lambs were slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The morning תמיד was slaughtered at the northwest corner, at the second ring. The afternoon תמיד was slaughtered at the northeast corner, also at the second ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The morning lamb was slaughtered at the northwest corner, at the second ring. The afternoon lamb was slaughtered at the northeast corner, at the second ring.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us the exact spot where each of the two daily תמיד lambs was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lambs used the second ring, but at different corners. The morning one was on the west side and the afternoon one on the east side.

keyTerms.meaning: Afternoon, the time of the second תמיד
A ring fixed in the floor, used to hold the animal during שחיטה

phrases.english: The morning one was slaughtered
at the northwest corner,
at the second ring.
The afternoon one was slaughtered
at the northeast corner,
at the second ring.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיָה נִשְׁחָט עַל קֶרֶן צְפוֹנִית מַעֲרָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from how the lamb was held to where it was slaughtered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Morning תמיד: northwest corner, second ring. Afternoon תמיד: northeast corner, second ring.

steps.title: Placing the blood on the altar and pouring out the rest
steps.stepSummary: After the שחיטה and the receiving of the blood, the כהן puts blood on the northeast corner so it reaches the east and north sides. Then he puts blood on the southwest corner so it reaches the west and south sides. He pours the leftover blood onto the southern יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The slaughterer slaughtered and the receiver received the blood. He comes to the northeast corner and places blood toward the east and north. Then he goes to the southwest corner and places blood toward the west and south. He would pour the rest of the blood onto the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the blood service of the תמיד, step by step, from receiving the blood to pouring out what remains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two placements of blood, made at two opposite corners. Each one reaches two sides of the מזבח, so together they cover all four sides. The leftover blood is not wasted: it is poured onto the southern יסוד.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן who receives the blood in a vessel
The leftover blood after the placements

steps.whatToRemember: The תמיד's blood is placed twice, at the northeast and southwest corners. Each placement reaches two sides, so all four sides are covered. The remaining blood goes onto the southern יסוד.

phrases.english: The slaughterer slaughtered, and the receiver received [the blood],
he comes to the northeast corner,
and places [it] toward the east and north.
[Then to the] southwest [corner],
and places [it] toward the west and south.
The rest of the blood,
he would pour onto the southern base.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט הַשּׁוֹחֵט, וְקִבֵּל הַמְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the שחיטה to the blood service.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood is placed at the northeast corner (reaching east and north) and at the southwest corner (reaching west and south). The remainder is poured on the southern יסוד.
